study: Murphy et al. 2020 (JREE), ASSISTments online math homework + teacher PD/coaching, Maine grade-7 RCT, 2nd-year outcomes (ERIC ED657283)
eval_evidence: Efficacy RCT conducted by SRI International (Robert Murphy et al.) under IES grant R305A120125; SRI is the independent third-party evaluator, distinct from ASSISTments' developer (WPI/Heffernan).
developer_evidence: The developer provided the PD: 'WPI hired a former math teacher and experienced ASSISTments user to provide professional development and technical assistance to teachers'; 'the ASSISTments team provided ample training and coaching to teachers.'
cascade_evidence: The WPI(developer)-hired trainer delivered the PD/coaching directly to treatment teachers; no train-the-trainer/lead-teacher intermediary hop.
counterfactual_evidence: Control = 'business as usual condition' (delayed access to ASSISTments; schools used their existing learning/homework practices); control schools given ASSISTments only after Year 2.
coaching_evidence: PD = 'a single two-day summer training and an additional day of technical assistance distributed across the school year via webinars, email, and in-person visits' (plus a 2nd summer session) -> light, mostly-remote periodic support, not recurring in-class coaching cycles.
student_dose_evidence: ASSISTments is an online math homework platform used directly by students (immediate per-item feedback as they do homework) = a substantial student-facing software dose, on top of the teacher PD/coaching and teacher performance reports.
maturity_evidence: Outcomes extracted from the SECOND implementation year (2013-14): treatment teachers used ASSISTments in Year 1, then again in Year 2 with a new grade-7 cohort whose outcomes were measured -> measured after >=1 prior implementation year (experienced teachers).
